items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: we got to be kind of buddy-buddy and run around together

ctx.x: Yeah, Earl Bostic. And so I still liked Spurgeon better as a band man than lead sax, but boy, I tell you, Earl Bostic blowed more horn, he was just a genius. I felt really close to Bostic.

The band director there, William Jett, in Tulsa High School when it started, he was from Hampton University, Hampton and Tuskegee are very closely related and we got to be kind of buddy-buddy and run around together, and he used to say to me, I'm going to have a good man for you--talking about Bostic--in the high school band--and he gave Bostic a clarinet and his dad was a junk man. Bostic goes home and was practicing the clarinet and his old man came in one day and the boy was practicing there and he picked up…
